title: Is it real coupling or volume conduction? The phase-lag index vs PLV, checked against scipy

dataset.name: EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database (eegmmidb)
dataset.record: subject S002, baseline run R02 (eyes-closed rest), occipital channels O1 and Oz, first 10 s at 160 Hz (1600 samples each)
dataset.citation: Schalk G, McFarland DJ, Hinterberger T, Birbaumer N, Wolpaw JR. BCI2000: a general-purpose brain-computer interface (BCI) system. IEEE Trans Biomed Eng 2004;51(6):1034-1043. EEG Motor Movement/Imagery Database, PhysioNet (Goldberger et al. 2000).

proposition: The sibling case found a high occipital alpha PLV (O1-Oz = 0.92) -- but is that genuine neural coupling, or just volume conduction (one source seen by two nearby electrodes, plus the common reference)? PLV can't tell: it counts zero-lag coupling as real. The phase-lag index (Stam 2007) can -- PLI = |mean(sign(sin(phi_x - phi_y)))| counts only a CONSISTENT non-zero phase lag, so it is ~0 for zero-lag coupling. On the SAME O1-Oz pair, the alpha PLI is just 0.016 -- the strong PLV collapses, revealing the 'synchronization' is dominated by near-zero-lag coupling (volume conduction). The measure is trustworthy: on constructed signals it recovers the contrast exactly (zero-lag -> PLV 0.99 but PLI 0.01; genuine lagged coupling -> PLI 1.0; independent -> both 0), it reproduces an independent scipy Hilbert-band PLI, and its sign formula is exact.

claims.statement: alpha-band (8-13 Hz) phase-lag index between occipital O1 and Oz -- volume-conduction-robust coupling (far below the 0.92 PLV)
max |phaseLagIndex - scipy Hilbert-band PLI| (agreement; PLI is sign-sensitive near zero-lag)
|op PLI - |mean(sign(sin(phase_diff)))|| -- the PLI sign formula, exact given the phases
PLV of constructed ZERO-LAG (common-source) signals -- PLV counts volume conduction, so it is high
PLI of the SAME zero-lag signals -- PLI correctly DISCOUNTS volume conduction, so it is ~0
PLI of constructed LAGGED (pi/4-offset) signals -- genuine non-zero-lag coupling, PLI ~ 1

validation.reference: PLI (Stam et al. 2007) is validated three ways. (1) Ground-truth contrast: on constructed signals, zero-lag coupling (a common source seen by both channels) gives PLV 0.99 but PLI 0.01 -- PLI discounts volume conduction; genuine lagged coupling (pi/4 offset) gives PLI 1.0; independent gives both ~0. (2) Cross-tool: an independent scipy Hilbert-band pipeline (butter+filtfilt+hilbert) gives the same PLI to ~4e-3. (3) The sign formula |mean(sign(sin(phase_diff)))| is exact given the phases. The finding: the real O1-Oz alpha PLI (0.016) is far below its PLV (0.92) -- the strong occipital alpha coupling is dominated by near-zero-lag / volume conduction.
validation.data: REAL -- eegmmidb (PhysioNet), S002 eyes-closed baseline R02, occipital O1 + Oz, 10 s at 160 Hz
validation.note: The reproducible findings are (1) phaseLagIndex recovers the volume-conduction contrast (zero-lag PLV 0.99 / PLI 0.01; lagged PLI 1.0; independent both ~0), reproduces an independent scipy Hilbert-band PLI (~4e-3), and its sign formula is exact; (2) the real O1-Oz alpha PLI (0.016) is far below the PLV (0.92). HONEST scope: (1) the scipy agreement is an AGREEMENT (~4e-3), NOT machine precision -- beyond the filtfilt-padding convention (shared with the PLV case), PLI's sign() is MORE sensitive near zero-lag, where tiny phase-difference differences flip the sign; the strong anchors are the EXACT sign formula and the ground-truth contrast; (2) the interpretation -- that the high O1-Oz PLV is mostly volume conduction -- is the textbook reason PLI/wPLI are preferred over PLV, demonstrated here on real data; but PLI is CONSERVATIVE: it discounts ALL near-zero-lag coupling, so a low PLI does not prove there is NO genuine interaction (true zero-lag neural coupling would also be discounted) -- it is a lower bound on lagged coupling, not a verdict; (3) descriptive, single subject/pair/band; run_simulation = FALSE (real-data PLI deterministic; the contrast is seeded).

open_questions.q: PLI is binary in the sign and can be noisy; the weighted PLI (weightedPLI, debiased, Vinck 2011 -- also implemented) weights each phase difference by |sin| and removes the sample-size bias, giving a less noisy volume-conduction-robust estimate. A full channel x channel wPLI matrix would map the genuinely-lagged posterior alpha network (as opposed to the volume-conduction-inflated PLV network), and contrasting eyes-closed vs eyes-open would test whether the lagged component tracks the rhythm. Documented, not escalated.
